Who to watch

Brown leaders (2026, through their last game)

  • Passing: #15 James Murphy — 182/283, 2065 yds, 7 TD, 11 INT
  • Rushing: #2 Matt Childs — 115 car, 456 yds, 7 TD
  • Receiving: #2 Matt Childs — 43 rec, 443 yds, 1 TD
  • Tackles: #10 Max Malo — 93
  • Sacks: #0 Ike Odimegwu — 6.5

Brown has won three straight: 38-31 in overtime over Cornell, 36-17 over Penn, and 24-20 at Yale on Nov. 7, Brown's first win over Yale since 2016 and first at the Yale Bowl since 2011 (Brown Athletics). At 5-3 and 3-2 in the league, the Bears are one game behind Harvard and Princeton (4-1). The defense allows 16.8 points a game. This is Brown's last home game of the season; the finale is at Dartmouth on Nov. 21 (ESPN).

Columbia leaders (2026, through their last game)

  • Passing: #15 Chase Goodwin — 175/323, 1960 yds, 14 TD, 11 INT
  • Rushing: #32 Griffin Johnson — 136 car, 614 yds, 3 TD
  • Receiving: #4 Bryce Coleman — 53 rec, 650 yds, 10 TD
  • Tackles: #18 AJ George — 64
  • Sacks: #0 Keller Patterson — 2.5

Columbia opened 4-1, with two overtime wins (Lafayette, Georgetown) and a 28-27 win at Penn, then lost three straight: Dartmouth 38-18, Yale 26-8 and Harvard 37-0, eight points in the last two games together. Freshman Bryce Coleman has 10 touchdown catches. Jon Poppe is in his third season as coach (ESPN box scores; Philadelphia Inquirer, Oct. 17; Columbia Athletics).

Ike Odimegwu

Defensive Lineman
6-3 · 240 lbs · Senior
Coppell, Texas (Coppell)
  • FCS Football Central Preseason All-America Second Team (Defense) (preseason).
  • Stats Perform FCS Preseason All-America Third Team (Defense) (preseason).
  • 2025 Second Team All-Ivy (Defense) (DL, ivyleague.com).

2026 so far

From the press

At Coppell High School in Texas, Odimegwu played both running back and defensive end; as a senior he scooped up a fumbled snap on a Hebron extra-point try and ran it back for two points in a 43-35 Heroes Night win. His Brown bio credits him with the 2022 District 6A Defensive MVP award and first-team all-area honors.

  • As a senior defensive end for Coppell High School on Heroes Night (Coppell 43, Hebron 35), he recovered a fumbled snap on a Hebron point-after attempt and returned it for two points; quoted afterward: "I wanted to be in the endzone." (The Sidekick / Coppell Student Media, Oct. 22, 2022)
  • Earlier in his Coppell career he lined up at running back, opening the scoring with a two-yard touchdown run in a homecoming win over the Wildcats. (The Sidekick / Coppell Student Media (game story, year not shown in index))
  • Named 2022 District 6A Defensive MVP and first-team all-area as a senior at Coppell, per his Brown roster bio. (Brown Athletics roster bio (brownbears.com, via search index; site not fetchable from here), 2025)

A Santa Cruz High product, Brown led the Bears with nine rushing touchdowns in 2024 and ran for 233 yards and five scores in 2025. He opened last season with two touchdowns against Georgetown, one of them a 49-yard run.

  • In Brown's 46-0 season-opening win over Georgetown on Sept. 20, 2025, he rushed nine times for 69 yards and two touchdowns, including a 49-yard scoring run late in the second quarter. (CBS Sports / AP, Sept. 20, 2025)
  • Appeared in all 10 games in 2025 and ranked second on the team with 233 rushing yards and five touchdowns; in 2024 he led the Bears with nine rushing touchdowns on 33 carries. (Brown Athletics roster bio (brownbears.com, via search index; site not fetchable from here), 2026)
  • As a Santa Cruz High running back he ran for 99 yards and a touchdown in a non-league win over Scotts Valley. (The Pajaronian (Watsonville, Calif.), c. 2021)

From the press

Childs was the 2024 Ivy League Rookie of the Year, leading Brown in rushing and scrimmage yards as a freshman, and followed it with a Second Team All-Ivy season in 2025 (517 rushing yards, eight touchdowns). At Milton Academy he was an All-NEPSAC pick and two-time ISL All-Star.

  • Named 2024 Ivy League Rookie of the Year: in nine games he led Brown in rushing and scrimmage yards with 361 rushing yards, 384 receiving yards and four total touchdowns, including a season-high 101 receiving yards and a touchdown against Harvard. (Ivy League release, Nov. 26, 2024)
  • Earned Ivy League Rookie of the Week honors in back-to-back weeks in October 2024. (Milton Academy news, 2024)
  • Named to Phil Steele's Freshman All-America fourth team after the 2024 season. (Brown Athletics news release, Dec. 20, 2024 (via search index))
  • At Milton Academy (class of 2024) he was an All-NEPSAC selection and two-time Independent School League All-Star; coach Mike Mason called him one of the best athletes he has coached. (Milton Academy news, 2024)
  • In 2025 he ran 137 times for 517 yards and eight touchdowns (ESPN) and earned Second Team All-Ivy League honors (WJAR Turn to 10). (ESPN player page; WJAR Turn to 10, 2025-26)

Bennett left Windermere Prep in Orlando holding 12 school records, among them 39 career touchdowns, and once scored seven times in a single game as a sophomore. His father played college football at Shepherd University; last season Bennett appeared in all 10 Brown games.

  • As a sophomore at Windermere Prep he scored seven touchdowns (four receiving, three rushing) against Trinity Prep on senior night, a school-record 42 points by one player; he also returned the season-opening kickoff for a touchdown and had early recruiting interest from North Carolina. (Spectrum News 13 (Orlando), Oct. 29, 2020)
  • In Week 2 of 2022 he ran for 249 yards on 13 carries with three touchdowns, the second-highest single-game rushing total in Windermere Prep history. (West Orange Times & Observer, Sept. 5, 2022)
  • Graduated as Windermere Prep's record holder in 12 statistical categories, including total yards (3,198), career rushing yards (2,351), career points (244) and total touchdowns (39); also played lacrosse. His father played college football at Shepherd University. (Brown Athletics roster bio (brownbears.com, via search index; site not fetchable from here), 2026)
  • Appeared in all 10 games for Brown in 2025, rushing 42 times for 161 yards and a touchdown. (Brown Athletics roster bio (brownbears.com, via search index; site not fetchable from here), 2026)

The series: Brown vs. Columbia

All-time: Brown leads 55-32-2 (Winsipedia). Columbia had won six of the eight meetings before Brown's 32-29 win last year (Columbia Athletics' 2025 preview, as indexed). Brown lost its last home meeting, 21-12, on Senior Day 2024 (Brown Athletics).

Last year, Nov. 15, 2025 at Columbia's Wien Stadium — Brown 32, Columbia 29. Columbia led 29-25 after Titus Evans's 8-yard catch with 4:07 left; Murphy then drove Brown down and found Matt Childs for 5 yards with 1:53 to go. Murphy threw for 340 and 4 touchdowns; Columbia's Michael Walters ran 27 times for 123 yards (ESPN).

Columbia scores: 2nd Beckett Robinson 24 yd pass from Chase Goodwin; 3rd Titus Evans 2 yd pass from Goodwin (2-pt good); 4th Michael Walters 1 yd run; 4th Evans 8 yd pass from Goodwin.
Brown scores: 1st Ty Pezza 7 yd pass from James Murphy (2-pt good); 2nd Pearson Hill 18 yd pass from Murphy; 3rd Drew Crabtree 23 yd field goal; 4th Matt Childs 10 and 5 yd passes from Murphy.

Game day

The stadium

Richard Gouse Field at Brown Stadium opened October 24, 1925, before 27,000 at the dedication. Capacity 20,000; the record crowd was 33,000 (Colgate, Thanksgiving 1932). FieldTurf since 2021, named for donor Richard I. Gouse '68. Ivy championship teams: 1976, 1999, 2005, 2008.

Saturday

  • Noon kickoff on ESPN+. Brown's last home game of 2026.
  • Brown has held Senior Day at its home finale against Columbia in 2018, 2022 and 2024 (Brown Athletics); this year's plans were not in any preview this tool could read.
  • Promotions and parking: check brownbears.com before you go.
